title: Speed up the slow queries
summary: Three queries behind the shop's busiest pages read whole tables. Add the right PostgreSQL indexes, and fix the query an index cannot help, so each one reads a few pages and returns the same rows.

checks.name: The migration runs
checks.description: indexes.sql runs without errors as the app's database user, on the empty tables, within 2 minutes, and leaves only indexes behind: the tables, columns and constraints stay as they are, and there are no new functions, views, triggers or other objects.

checks.name: Order history
checks.description: For random customers (large, regular, small, and one with two orders at the same time among its newest), queries/orders_for_customer.sql returns the same rows in the same order as the original query, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows it reading at most 60 pages, with no sequential scan.

checks.name: Find a customer by email
checks.description: For 5 random email addresses in random upper and lower case, one of them shared by two customers and one unknown, queries/find_customer.sql returns the same rows as the original query and reads at most 20 pages, with no sequential scan.

checks.name: Revenue for a day
checks.description: For 4 random days, one of them with no orders, queries/revenue_for_day.sql returns the same totals as the original query and reads at most 200 pages, with no sequential scan.
